case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Reversing a one-page order dismissing an abuse and neglect petition, the Court held that a circuit court that sees reasonable cause to believe additional abuse or neglect exists may compel DHHR to investigate and amend the petition, and must enter findings of fact and conclusions of law on the allegations.
key_cases.relevance: It reverses a dismissal entered without evidentiary findings.
key_cases.quote: the circuit court has the inherent authority to compel the Department to amend its petition to encompass the evidence or allegations

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Vacating the adjudicatory and dispositional orders, the Court held that a Rule 26(a) stipulated adjudication must contain agreed facts supporting court involvement and a statement of the respondent's problems, and that without a proper adjudication the circuit court had no jurisdiction to proceed to disposition.
key_cases.relevance: Where adjudication was defective, the resulting orders are vacated and the case returns to the circuit court.
key_cases.quote: Without properly made findings of abuse and/or neglect at adjudication, a case cannot proceed to disposition

key_cases.case_name: In the Interest of Tiffany Marie S.
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Affirming a finding of abuse and neglect, the Court held that a circuit court's findings of fact in an abuse and neglect case may be disturbed only if clearly erroneous, while its conclusions of law are reviewed de novo, and that the Department must prove the conditions existing when the petition was filed by clear and convincing proof.
key_cases.relevance: Dismissal or non-substantiation rulings will stand unless the reviewing court is firmly convinced a mistake was made.
key_cases.quote: absent a mistake of law, an appellate tribunal should disturb a circuit court's determination only if it is clearly erroneous

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Remanding for a proper adjudicatory hearing, the Court held that a circuit court may not reach any dispositional alternative until it has held a hearing and determined whether the child is abused or neglected, and that a voluntary arrangement among the parties cannot bypass that threshold question.
key_cases.relevance: If the evidence is insufficient to warrant a finding of abuse or neglect, the statute directs the court to dismiss the petition.
key_cases.quote: have determined "whether such child is abused or neglected." Such a finding is the prerequisite to any further proceedings in the case.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Vacating both dispositional orders, the Court held that the fifteen-of-twenty-two-months filing trigger does not relieve the Department of presenting, or the circuit court of finding, affirmative evidence supporting termination, and that the court lacked subject matter jurisdiction over a child who did not meet the statutory definition of an abused or neglected child.
key_cases.relevance: Where the statutory definition of an abused or neglected child is not met, the orders as to that child are vacated for want of jurisdiction and the matter returns to the circuit court.
key_cases.quote: Because B.S. was not an abused or neglected child, the circuit court lacked subject matter jurisdiction to address, and ultimately terminate, the petitioner's parental rights to this child

key_cases.case_name: In re E.H., J.S., E.K., and C.K.
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Vacating the dispositional order and remanding, the Court held that an order terminating parental rights that lacks the findings of fact and conclusions of law required by Rule 36(a) and W. Va. Code § 49-4-604 cannot support termination and must be vacated.
key_cases.relevance: A disposition entered without the findings the rules require is set aside in its entirety and the case returned to the circuit court for a proper order.
key_cases.quote: we agree with Petitioner that the December 27, 2021 dispositional order does not contain the requisite findings of fact or conclusions of law to support termination of his parental rights
